text: In 1985 the Crown charged Zündel, the publisher of Did Six Million Really Die?, with spreading false news. His conviction was overturned when the case reached the Supreme Court of Canada.

sources.title: Wikipedia: R v Zundel
sources.quote: In 1985 the Crown took over the case and Zündel was charged with "spreading false news" by publishing the pamphlet

sources.title: Wikipedia: R v Zundel
sources.quote: When Zündel's case reached the Supreme Court of Canada, his conviction was overturned.

note: Prosecution of the publisher under Criminal Code s.181 (false news), not a ban of the pamphlet itself. Wikipedia article; SCC judgment page (scc-csc.lexum.com) returned 403. Germany/South Africa bans: only Wikipedia's one-line claim citing Wyman & Rosenzveig 1996 p.682; no dated primary source reachable.

text: In 1940 an Oklahoma City police detective bought copies of Lenin's The State and Revolution at a bookstore. Police then raided the store and seized more than 10,000 books.

sources.title: Oklahoma Gazette: Bookstore arrests of the forties presaged communist scare
sources.quote: On July 24, 1940, an Oklahoma City police detective dressed as an oil field worker walked into the bookstore, and purchased copies of: ” Vladimir Lenin’s “The State and Revolution,”

sources.title: Oklahoma Gazette: Bookstore arrests of the forties presaged communist scare
sources.quote: On Aug. 17, police raided the store, arresting about 20 people ” including customers ” and seized more than 10,000 books.

note: Oklahoma Gazette 2007 article on the Progressive Bookstore case (Wiegand, Books on Trial). Seizure of stock including this title; the source does not say the book itself was burned.

text: In 1927 the North Dakota State Library decided not to stock Elmer Gantry. In Boston, sales of the novel could be prosecuted under a law prohibiting indecent and obscene books.

sources.title: Banning Elmer Gantry (Dakota Datebook, Prairie Public, 4 Jun 2022)
sources.quote: On this date in 1927, North Dakotans joined in censoring Elmer Gantry when the North Dakota State Library decided not to stock it.

sources.title: Dakota Datebook, same page
sources.quote: banned in some areas around the country, such as Boston, where sales of Elmer Gantry could be prosecuted under a law prohibiting 'indecent and obscene books.'

note: Boston prosecution threat dated 13 April 1927 per NYT headline 'Boston Bans Sale of Elmer Gantry' (cited by Wikipedia, article itself not fetched); Wikipedia: banned in Boston and other cities.

text: In 1984 a parent petitioned against the use of The Color Purple in an Oakland, California classroom, and the Oakland schools ultimately decided not to remove the book from classrooms. In 2013 a parent challenged the book in Brunswick County, North Carolina.

sources.title: Why parents still try to ban 'The Color Purple' in schools (National Geographic, 22 Aug 2023)
sources.quote: The first major attempt to ban the book occurred in 1984, when a parent petitioned against its use in an Oakland, California classroom.

sources.title: National Geographic, same article
sources.quote: Though the Oakland schools ultimately decided not to remove the book from classrooms, the book has consistently been challenged nationwide since its publication

sources.title: National Geographic, same article
sources.quote: “One can eat from a cafeteria or a dumpster…but one would hope those placed in charge of our children would have exercised better oversight,” wrote one parent in a characteristic 2013 challenge in Brunswick County, North Carolina.

note: Oakland 1984 matches our US 1984 'rescinded' row (challenge, book retained). Israel 2012 row is the author declining publication (BDS), not a state or institutional ban; South Africa row is about the film, per its own note.

text: On 5 October 1988 India banned the novel's importation, after Syed Shahabuddin petitioned the government of Rajiv Gandhi. In November 1988 it was also banned in Bangladesh, Sudan and South Africa, and by December 1988 in Sri Lanka. In March 1989 it was banned in Kenya, Thailand, Tanzania, Indonesia and Singapore, and the last nation to ban it was Venezuela, in June 1989.

sources.title: Satanic Verses controversy, timeline (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: 5 October 1988: India bans the novel's importation, after Indian parliamentarian and editor of the monthly magazine Muslim India Syed Shahabuddin petitioned the government of Rajiv Gandhi to ban the book.

sources.title: Satanic Verses controversy, Wikipedia (cites Netton, Pipes)
sources.quote: In November 1988, it was also banned in Bangladesh , Sudan , and South Africa. By December 1988, it was also banned in Sri Lanka .

sources.title: Satanic Verses controversy, Wikipedia
sources.quote: March 1989 saw it banned in Kenya, Thailand, Tanzania, Indonesia, and Singapore. [ 11 ] The last nation to ban the book was Venezuela, in June 1989.

note: Wikipedia article; quotes are from a plain-text strip with spaces around inline links. Consistent with our rows (Sudan, South Africa Nov 1988; Sri Lanka by Dec 1988; Thailand Mar 1989; Venezuela Jun 1989). Not verified here: Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi, Somalia, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar rows.

text: In April 2025 the Lukashenko regime added the book to a list of printed publications whose distribution could harm the national interests of Belarus.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
sources.quote: In April 2025, the Lukashenko regime added the book to the list of printed publications containing information messages and materials, the distribution of which could harm the national interests of Belarus

note: Wikipedia cites a euroradio.fm report of 1 April 2025.

text: In a report dated 10 November 2013, the All Pakistan Private Schools Federation, which says it represents more than 152,000 institutions, decided against letting pupils read I Am Malala. The book was not to be included in the schools' curriculum or stocked in school libraries.

sources.title: The Independent: Private schools in Pakistan ban Malala Yousafzai's book
sources.quote: The All Pakistan Private Schools Federation, which says it represents more than 152,000 institutions across the country, has decided that allowing pupils to read the book, I am Malala , would have a "negative" effect on them.

sources.title: The Independent (date line)
sources.quote: Umair Aziz & Andrew Buncombe Sunday 10 November 2013 00:00 GMT

sources.title: The Independent
sources.quote: The book will not be included in the schools' curriculum, nor will it be stocked in school libraries.

note: Private-school federation measure, not a state ban.

text: In 1775 both the novel and the Werther clothing style were banned in Leipzig, and the novel was also banned in Denmark and Italy (no date given for those two).

sources.title: Wikipedia: The Sorrows of Young Werther
sources.quote: both the novel and the Werther clothing style were banned in Leipzig in 1775; the novel was also banned in Denmark and Italy.

note: Wikipedia footnote 12; Italy and Denmark undated. No source found for the Austria 1775 row.

text: The Australian Minister of Customs drew up a list of 128 publications in December 1927 and submitted it to the Federal Parliament as prohibited, seized and forfeited; the list includes The Communist Manifesto.

sources.title: The Censor in Australia (Socialist Standard, February 1929)
sources.quote: The Australian Minister of Customs drew up, in December, 1927, and submitted to the Federal Parliament a list of 128 publications which are “prohibited, seized and forfeited.” During 1928 some 40 publications were added to the list. It includes such works as “ The Communist Manifesto, ”

note: 1929 secondary account (citing Labour Monthly, January 1929); Australian import prohibition, not among our rows. Could not source NZ/ZA/AR/PT/DE rows in fetched pages.

text: In early March 2026, bookstore co-founder Artem Faustov was fined 50,000 rubles for selling Beartown.

sources.title: OC Media: Makhachkala bookshop fined for LGBT propaganda in books by Le Guin and Backman
sources.quote: The Leninsky District Court in Makhachkala fined the bookstore chain, Chitai-Gorod, on 16 March, according to Russian independent media outlet Mediazona

sources.title: OC Media (same article)
sources.quote: According to the case materials, the grounds for the protocol were the books Beartown and Us Against You by Swedish author Fredrik Backman

sources.title: The Insider: In Putin's bad book
sources.quote: in early March 2026, Artem Faustov, co-founder of the bookstore Vse Svobodny, was fined 50,000 rubles ($670) for selling Fredrik Backman’s Beartown even though an expert review by the Russian Book Union had concluded that the book contained nothing prohibited.

note: Makhachkala ruling is 16 March (2026 per context; year not in quote). Penalties fell on booksellers, not the publisher.

text: In France, Lolita was banned as a "dangerous book" until 1958. On September 17, 1958, the Cincinnati Public Library banned Lolita.

sources.title: Nabokov at Cornell: Publishing Lolita
sources.quote: The book's appearance sparked a flurry of publicity in France, where it was banned as a "dangerous book" until 1958.

sources.title: Nabokov at Cornell: Publishing Lolita (same page)
sources.quote: On September 17, 1958, the Cincinnati Public Library banned Lolita.

note: Cornell page says France ban lasted until 1958; our row has France 1956-onward (lifted 1958/59), consistent.

text: In an interview published on September 30, 1997, Arundhati Roy was reported to face obscenity charges in Kerala brought by an individual lawyer, Sabu Thomas. She said she had appealed to the high court, and they decided to give the case to a lower court.

sources.title: Salon: The Salon Interview: Arundhati Roy
sources.quote: The Salon Interview: Arundhati Roy. The author of 'The God of Small Things' talks about India, the obscenity charge she faces and how writing is like architecture. By Reena Jana. By Reena Jana Published September 30, 1997 7:00PM (EDT)

sources.title: Salon interview (same page)
sources.quote: The obscenity charges brought forth by an individual lawyer, Sabu Thomas, that you face are in Kerala, the same Indian region you depict in your book.

sources.title: Salon interview (same page)
sources.quote: In fact, last week, I made an appeal to the high court, and they decided to give the case to a lower court.

note: Prosecution (criminal obscenity charge) against the book/author, not a ban; no ban recorded. Outcome not sourced.

text: The book was challenged in Wasilla, Alaska, after a boy picked it up from the juvenile non-fiction shelf of the public library, in a report dated 26 Nov 2015. In a survey reported on 19 Aug 2024, Index on Censorship said 53% of librarians polled had been asked to remove books, and This Book Is Gay by Juno Dawson was among the titles complained about.

sources.title: Parents in Alaska challenge decision to keep it on library shelves (The Guardian)
sources.quote: The book has been challenged in Wasilla, Alaska, after a 10-year-old boy picked it up from the juvenile non-fiction shelf of the public library

sources.title: same article (date line)
sources.quote: Alaska challenge decision to keep it on library shelves Alison Flood Thu 26 Nov 2015 18.06 CET

sources.title: Dozens of UK school librarians asked to remove LGBTQ+ books, survey finds (The Guardian)
sources.quote: Index on Censorship said 53% of librarians polled had been asked to remove books – and that in more than half of those cases books were taken off shelves Ella Creamer Mon 19 Aug 2024

sources.title: same article
sources.quote: Among the titles complained about were This Book Is Gay by Juno Dawson, Julián is a Mermaid by Jessica Love, and ABC Pride by Louie Stowell

text: In January 2023 the book was permanently banned from libraries and classrooms in St. Johns County School District, and in September 2023 it was banned from libraries and classrooms in Matanuska-Susitna Borough School District.

sources.title: Call Me by Your Name (novel) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: In January 2023, the book was permanently banned from libraries and classrooms in St. Johns County School District

sources.title: Call Me by Your Name (novel) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: In September 2023, the book was banned from libraries and classrooms in Matanuska-Susitna Borough School District

note: Wikipedia cites PEN America's school book ban indexes 2022-23 and 2023-24. Also read: The Bell (en.thebell.io/russia-bans-books-mentioning-lgbt-issues/, dated 6 Dec 2022) says online store Labirint hid books by Andre Aciman including Call Me by Your Name amid LGBT-related removals; supports our Russia 2022 row but not used as quote because the year is not in the passage.

text: In 1985 a group of Islamists won an injunction removing the book from the market in Egypt, and a year later a higher court reversed the decision.

sources.title: The Arabian Nights: Obscene Pornography or a Great Work of Culture? (Qantara, Samir Grees)
sources.quote: It's not the first time that The Arabian Nights have led to angry debate in Egypt. In 1985, a group of Islamists managed to win an injunction removing the book from the market. A year later, a higher court reversed the decision.

note: Matches our Egypt 1985-86 rescinded row. Casanova Society NZ restriction on Wikipedia's NZ list has no year in the table text, so not used.

text: The novel was placed on the Index in 1834.

sources.title: Notre-Dame de Paris (roman) - Wikipédia
sources.quote: Considéré comme une lecture pernicieuse par l'Église catholique, Notre-Dame de Paris fait partie des romans mis à l' Index en 1834

note: French Wikipedia states the 1834 Index listing; footnote text not recovered. Quote contains 'l' Index' with a space from the wikilink rendering. English Wikipedia's Index list says 'Until 1959' for Hugo's Notre Dame de Paris, which conflicts with our row end year 1966 (Index discontinued 1966; 1959 unsourced there).
